record.original_question: Further develop algorithmic information theory for bi-infinite sequences and, more generally, for constructive cpo's, possibly using bi-infinite cellular automata as computational models.

evidence.quote: 12. Further develop algorithmic information theory for bi-infinite sequences and, more generally, for constructive cpo's. (C. Calude, H. Jürgensen) An idea would be to use bi-infinite cellular automata as computational models. (F. Geurts)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a theory of algorithmic information (Kolmogorov/Chaitin complexity, randomness, and related notions) for bi-infinite sequences over a finite alphabet, i.e., elements of $\Sigma^{\mathbb{Z}}$, and more generally for constructive complete partial orders (cpo's). 

Concretely, the task is to:

1. Define a suitable notion of descriptive (Kolmogorov-style) complexity $K(x)$ for a bi-infinite sequence $x \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{Z}}$, together with a corresponding notion of algorithmic randomness, in such a way that the basic invariance, incompressibility, and characterization theorems known for one-sided infinite sequences (Martin-Löf randomness, prefix complexity characterizations, etc.) carry over in an appropriate form.

2. Extend this construction from $\Sigma^{\mathbb{Z}}$ to arbitrary constructive complete partial orders: produce a uniform definition of complexity and randomness for elements of an effectively given cpo, and prove the analogues of the standard theorems (existence of universal machines, invariance up to additive constants, characterization of random elements via constructive null sets, etc.).

3. Investigate whether bi-infinite cellular automata — i.e., shift-commuting continuous maps $F : \Sigma^{\mathbb{Z}} \to \Sigma^{\mathbb{Z}}$ given by a local rule — can serve as a natural class of computational models underlying this theory, in the way that Turing machines underlie the classical theory, and determine which complexity- and randomness-theoretic notions admit equivalent formulations in terms of such automata.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a programmatic open direction posed in a list of open problems in algorithmic information theory. Some related work has been carried out (e.g., metrics on bi-infinite sequence spaces inspired by information distance, and studies of randomness generation in cellular automata by Calude, Hertling, Jürgensen, Weihrauch and collaborators), but no comprehensive algorithmic information theory for bi-infinite sequences and constructive cpo's based on bi-infinite cellular automata appears to have been established. The direction remains broadly open.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic Information Theory: Open Problems (CDMTCS Research Report)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists problem 12: develop AIT for bi-infinite sequences and constructive cpo's, possibly via bi-infinite cellular automata.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic Information Theory and Cellular Automata Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the space of bi-infinite sequences with a metric inspired by Kolmogorov information distance and cellular automata dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Partial related work exists but does not constitute a full AIT for cpo's.
